D3_r3_4_apply_local.verdict: CONFIRMED — the hazard is real and measured, not hypothetical
measured_hazard: scripts/stella-r3-4-local-runner.ts:120-127 — apply iterates R3_4_LOCAL_PHASES in order with NO enclosing transaction across phases
scripts/stella-r3-4-local-runner.ts:83-91 — runAdministrativePhase COMMITS its own client.sql.begin() block and logs 'committed administrative phase' per phase

db/r3-4-governed-runner.ts:26-42 — stella_0001_role_topology_bootstrap.sql is the THIRD phase, preceded by two already-committing administrative phases (stella_0002_interactions_hardening.sql, stella_0002b_append_only_truncate_hardening.sql)
D3_r3_4_apply_local.why_this_is_the_defect: Because each phase commits independently, a stella_0001 failure caused by absent successor preconditions occurs AFTER two prepared phases have already committed. The run is then neither applied nor clean. This is exactly the condition the successor contract must make unreachable.
D3_r3_4_apply_local.required_invariant: SUCCESSOR PRECONDITIONS ABSENT -> non-zero exit -> ZERO prepared mutation occurred.
D3_r3_4_apply_local.placement_requirement: The precondition probe must execute BEFORE the phase loop begins — before the first prepared mutation of any phase, not before stella_0001 only.
D3_r3_4_apply_local.narrowness_requirement: Prefer a narrow, repository-native precondition probe. Do NOT duplicate every stella_0001 assertion. The probe must cover exactly the minimal_preflight_facts enumerated below and nothing more. A probe that checks the two schema privileges and nothing else does NOT satisfy this invariant: the grantor and ADMIN-option facts are the load-bearing ones, and were the actual measured failure mode (see D5_b2_grantor.measured_prebaseline_probe control N).
minimal_preflight_facts: 1. The five uellix_* roles exist (uellix_owner, uellix_migrator, uellix_app, uellix_writer, uellix_auditor).

2. No relevant pg_auth_members row has grantor <> oid 10. RELEVANT means the same row set stella_0001's own canonical membership precondition selects: member IN (uellix_app, uellix_writer, uellix_migrator) OR roleid IN (uellix_app, uellix_writer, uellix_owner, uellix_migrator).
3. No relevant pg_auth_members row has admin_option = true.
D3_r3_4_apply_local.minimal_preflight_facts_basis: Facts 2 and 3 are not stylistic. MEASURED against the exact pinned disposable image: running stella_0001's own precondition block verbatim against a topology installed by postgres raised 'stella_0001 FAILED: canonical membership precondition rejected unexpected relevant membership row (wrong grantor, flags or ADMIN escalation)' listing all seven rows — four ADMIN-option auto-grant rows plus three grantor=postgres(oid=16384) memberships. The same block exits 0 against a supabase_admin-installed topology. A preflight omitting facts 2-3 would let exactly that failure occur AFTER two prepared phases had already committed, which is the condition required_invariant exists to make unreachable.
D3_r3_4_apply_local.probe_semantics: READ ONLY. Executes BEFORE the first prepared mutation of any phase. FAIL CLOSED. NO REPAIR.
D3_r3_4_apply_local.fail_closed_requirement: The probe fails closed. On an indeterminate result it must refuse, never proceed. It must not repair, re-grant or provision anything — it observes and refuses.

D4_r3_5_historical_certification.consequence: The P1A successor contract modifies db/prepared/stella_0001_role_topology_bootstrap.sql (converting the canonical grants at :176 and :181 into fail-closed assertions). That changes its bytes, so the live pin will no longer match current HEAD.
D4_r3_5_historical_certification.FORBIDDEN: db/r3-5-pg17-certification-inputs.ts MUST NOT be repinned, edited or regenerated to match the new bytes. Updating a historical hash to agree with bytes the historical run never executed would manufacture a false certification. It is not in the authorized surface of this amendment and is not authorized by any other clause here.
D4_r3_5_historical_certification.REQUIRED: The current R3.5 command and its test must explicitly report SUPERSEDED for current HEAD where the historical pin no longer matches, rather than throwing an undifferentiated SHA mismatch or silently repinning. SUPERSEDED must be distinguishable from both PASS and an ordinary integrity failure.
D4_r3_5_historical_certification.REQUIRED_PLACEMENT: The throw itself lives in db/r3-5-pg17-certification-inputs.ts, which this amendment declares BYTE-IMMUTABLE and forbids editing. The SUPERSEDED disposition MUST therefore be classified in the authorized path — scripts/stella-r3-5-pg17-certify.ts, at or before the loadVerifiedR3Sources() call sites :544/:549 — BEFORE delegating into the historical mismatch throw. Classifying ahead of the delegation is not a bypass: assertR3_5Pg17CertificationSourceHashes stays byte-identical, keeps its full strength for every other file, and continues to fail closed for any divergence that is not the adjudicated SUPERSEDED case. Editing db/r3-5-pg17-certification-inputs.ts to add the disposition would be a repin of historical evidence by another name, and is NOT authorized.
D4_r3_5_historical_certification.successor_relationship: P1A is a SUCCESSOR_OF the historical R3.5 PostgreSQL 17 certification. Successor is not equivalence: it records that the historical proof covered the predecessor bytes and that the successor bytes are a distinct object requiring their own proof.

measured_prebaseline_probe.key_finding: postgres is ALREADY NOSUPERUSER in the native pre-baseline image. db/baseline/stella_g2_roles.sql:39 does not create that state; it re-asserts it. Pre-baseline and post-baseline attributes are therefore IDENTICAL for both actors, and supabase_admin is oid 10 at both instants.

D5_b2_grantor.correction_postgres_can_grant: RETRACTED CLAIM. The previous revision stated that 'a membership GRANT attempted as postgres FAILS'. That is FALSE and is withdrawn. MEASURED: postgres (NOSUPERUSER, CREATEROLE) successfully created all five uellix_* roles and successfully issued all three memberships, including uellix_writer TO postgres. PostgreSQL 16+ automatically grants the creating CREATEROLE role membership WITH ADMIN OPTION over every role it creates, which is sufficient. supabase_admin is required for the three reasons below, NOT because postgres is incapable.
three_measured_reasons_supabase_admin_is: REASON 1 — GRANTOR PIN. db/prepared/stella_0001_role_topology_bootstrap.sql §2 pins the canonical grantor as oid 10 for the relevant membership rows and refuses any unexpected relevant row. MEASURED: supabase_admin IS oid 10, so a grant it issues records grantor=10; a grant issued by postgres records grantor=16384. Running stella_0001's precondition block VERBATIM against a postgres-installed topology raised 'stella_0001 FAILED: canonical membership precondition rejected unexpected relevant membership row (wrong grantor, flags or ADMIN escalation)' and exited 3. Against a supabase_admin-installed topology the same block exits 0.

REASON 2 — ADMIN-OPTION AUTO-GRANTS / RR-02. MEASURED: when postgres (CREATEROLE non-superuser) creates the five roles, PostgreSQL 16+ emits five automatic membership rows granting postgres each role WITH admin_option=true. When supabase_admin (a superuser) creates the same five roles, the auto-grant row count is ZERO. Those five rows are themselves rejected by stella_0001's precondition, and they reproduce RR-02 locally: MEASURED, postgres then granted itself uellix_owner WITH SET TRUE and SET ROLE uellix_owner succeeded. Under the supabase_admin installer the same attempt is refused with 'permission denied to grant role "uellix_owner" — Only roles with the ADMIN option on role "uellix_owner" may grant this role.' The local separation is a BARRIER under supabase_admin and merely an auditable obstacle under postgres.

REASON 3 — AUTH-SCHEMA FAIL-OPEN. MEASURED: GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA auth TO uellix_owner issued as postgres emits 'WARNING: no privileges were granted for "auth"', prints GRANT, and EXITS 0 — while has_schema_privilege('uellix_owner','auth','USAGE') remains false. It is a silent no-op that ON_ERROR_STOP=1 cannot catch, because a WARNING is not an ERROR. Issued as supabase_admin (the owner of schema auth) the same statement succeeds and the privilege is present.

actor_partition.statement: The previous revision resolved EVERY v1.0.0 'local administrative superuser' operation to supabase_admin. That over-resolved: it would have enlarged the supabase_admin write surface for zero catalog effect and made the P1A-N7 closed world indeterminate. The partition below is frozen instead, and it is what makes P1A_N7_EXACT_COUNT = 3 closed-world rather than 5.
supabase_admin_performs: creation of the five uellix_* roles (CREATE ROLE x5)
membership A — GRANT uellix_owner TO uellix_migrator
membership B — GRANT uellix_writer TO uellix_app
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA auth TO uellix_owner
postgres_retains: GRANT USAGE, CREATE ON SCHEMA public TO uellix_owner
REVOKE CREATE ON SCHEMA public FROM uellix_migrator, uellix_app, uellix_writer, uellix_auditor, PUBLIC
actor_partition.why_postgres_retains_the_public_schema_a: MEASURED: schema public is owned by pg_database_owner, and the resulting ACL entry is byte-identical under both actors — uellix_owner=UC/pg_database_owner — because the grant is attributed to the schema owner, not to the issuing role. Routing these two statements through supabase_admin therefore produces NO catalog difference while enlarging the superuser surface. The single-write discipline P1A-N7 exists to enforce forbids that trade.
actor_partition.local_administrative_superuser_identity: Wherever v1.0.0 canonical_privilege_sequence names the actor 'local administrative superuser', it resolves to supabase_admin ONLY for the operations enumerated in supabase_admin_performs above. It does NOT resolve to supabase_admin for the public-schema ACL operations, which postgres both can and must continue to issue.

D6_p1a_n7.previous_rule: P1A-N7 as frozen in v1.0.0 (line 448) and in the test manifest: 'No unauthorized privilege write under supabase_admin outside the one explicitly governed auth-schema capability: a per-container call-count invariant proves exactly one such write per fixture.'
D6_p1a_n7.amended_rule: EXACTLY THREE enumerated supabase_admin privilege writes in the local bootstrap package, and no others.
D6_p1a_n7.SUPABASE_ADMIN_PRIVILEGE_WRITE_DEFINITIO: A statement executed with session_user AND current_user equal to supabase_admin that MUTATES THE PRIVILEGE GRAPH — that is, it inserts, updates or deletes a pg_auth_members row (role membership GRANT/REVOKE), or it modifies an object ACL (GRANT/REVOKE on a schema, table, function, database or other privilege-bearing object). This definition is the counting domain. It is stated explicitly because the previous revision said only 'STATEMENTS issued under the supabase_admin actor', which would have swept in CREATE ROLE and role-attribute statements and made the count indeterminate.

enumerated_writes.statement: GRANT uellix_owner TO uellix_migrator WITH INHERIT FALSE, SET TRUE, ADMIN FALSE
enumerated_writes.reason_actor_is_supabase_admin: grantor must be oid 10 for stella_0001's canonical precondition, and supabase_admin creation avoids the ADMIN-option auto-grant rows that same precondition rejects

enumerated_writes.statement: GRANT uellix_writer TO uellix_app WITH INHERIT TRUE, SET FALSE, ADMIN FALSE
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA auth TO uellix_owner
enumerated_writes.basis: v1.0.0 canonical_topology PHASE_BOOTSTRAP_PRIVILEGE and canonical_privilege_sequence step 4; inherited from scripts/m2-disposable-pg-bootstrap.ts:645-656; D5_b2_grantor three_measured_reasons REASON 3
enumerated_writes.reason_actor_is_supabase_admin: supabase_admin owns schema auth; MEASURED, the same statement as postgres is a silent WARNING no-op that exits 0 and grants nothing

explicitly_excluded_from_the_count.excluded: CREATE ROLE x5 (uellix_owner, uellix_migrator, uellix_app, uellix_writer, uellix_auditor), issued by supabase_admin
explicitly_excluded_from_the_count.why: MEASURED: a SUPERUSER creating a role emits ZERO pg_auth_members rows and no ACL — auto-grant row count was 0. It creates a principal, it does not mutate the privilege graph, so it falls outside SUPABASE_ADMIN_PRIVILEGE_WRITE_DEFINITION. (The contrast is exactly REASON 2: a CREATEROLE non-superuser creating the same roles emits five admin_option=true rows, which WOULD be privilege-graph mutations.)

explicitly_excluded_from_the_count.excluded: ALTER ROLE uellix_auditor SET default_transaction_read_only = on
explicitly_excluded_from_the_count.why: A per-role GUC default. It confers and removes no privilege and touches no ACL or membership row.

explicitly_excluded_from_the_count.excluded: GRANT USAGE, CREATE ON SCHEMA public TO uellix_owner; and REVOKE CREATE ON SCHEMA public FROM uellix_migrator, uellix_app, uellix_writer, uellix_auditor, PUBLIC;
explicitly_excluded_from_the_count.why: These ARE privilege-graph mutations, but they are NOT issued by supabase_admin. Per D5_b2_grantor actor_partition they remain with postgres, because the resulting ACL was MEASURED byte-identical under both actors (uellix_owner=UC/pg_database_owner, attributed to the pg_database_owner schema owner rather than the issuing role). Moving them under supabase_admin would add two supabase_admin privilege writes for zero catalog effect.

explicitly_excluded_from_the_count.excluded: GRANT uellix_writer TO postgres WITH INHERIT TRUE, SET FALSE, ADMIN FALSE (membership C)
explicitly_excluded_from_the_count.why: Not issued by the local bootstrap package at all. It is owned by db/prepared/stella_0001_role_topology_bootstrap.sql §2 — see membership_c_disposition below. It is therefore NOT a fourth local-package supabase_admin privilege write.

membership_c_disposition.membership: uellix_writer TO postgres WITH INHERIT TRUE, SET FALSE, ADMIN FALSE
membership_c_disposition.NOT_legacy: It is part of the canonical reference topology: db/baseline/stella_g2_roles.sql:222 carries it as GRANT uellix_writer TO postgres WITH INHERIT TRUE, SET FALSE GRANTED BY supabase_admin. It gives postgres INHERITED writer rights and is a live element of the topology, not residue.
membership_c_disposition.NOT_removed: This amendment does not delete, deprecate or narrow it. It remains established by db/prepared/stella_0001_role_topology_bootstrap.sql §2, whose conditional REVOKE/re-GRANT pair is its single mutating authority.
membership_c_disposition.NOT_part_of_local_package_N7: MEASURED: stella_0001's canonical membership precondition is a 'no UNEXPECTED relevant row' guard, not an 'all expected rows present' guard. Running it verbatim against a supabase_admin-installed topology with membership C ABSENT exits 0. C therefore need not exist before stella_0001, and the local package must not establish it.
membership_c_disposition.NOT_a_fourth_supabase_admin_write: Because stella_0001 is applied under the R3.4 administrative identity, which asserts a superuser session and on this substrate resolves to supabase_admin (oid 10), C is issued with the grantor its own precondition expects on the next run. It is a stella_0001 statement, not a local-package statement, and it does not enter the P1A-N7 count.

D6_p1a_n7.no_wildcard: This is a CLOSED-WORLD enumeration of exactly three statements in the local bootstrap package.
